Numerical deviations of the model from the measurements of Sr-90
Register rows of Sr-90 (including rows labelled with the element only): 101; 53 digitised from published figures (labelled digitised, with their reading uncertainty), 48 tabulated or printed
and exact as printed.
Comparison status of these rows: NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE 101.
NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE because the measured quantity is not the model quantity: 29 x failed_or_released_particles (failed SiC or releasing particle); 1 x fuel_sphere (fuel sphere of a
benchmark); 23 x includes_in_pile_inventory (total includes in-pile inventory); 21 x irradiation_phase_quantity (irradiation-phase inventory location); 16 x loose_particles_with_failures
(loose particles including failed ones); 11 x other_fuel_batch (AGR-2 fuel).
No Sr-90 row supports a point comparison, so the absolute deviation, the relative deviation in percent and the log-space root-mean-square deviation are not defined for Sr-90; no number is
substituted.

Experimental values: Collin et al. (2016); IAEA (2012); Stempien et al. (2023). Only the rows whose status supports a comparison are drawn in colour; rows that are NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE are muted grey context,

because they measure another quantity than the model computes (failed particles, totals that include release in the reactor, another fuel, fuel spheres). A bar on a marker is the reading uncertainty of the register

(the error of reading the point off the published figure); it is not a measurement uncertainty, and the sources report no per-value measurement uncertainty for these rows (a general 5 percent systematic

gamma-measurement error stated for the Stempien 2023 values is not a per-value uncertainty and changes no status), so no other error bar is drawn. Compact values are not single-particle values; rows at a temperature
outside 1600 to 1800 °C or whose value is not a fraction are not drawn. Not drawn because the time at temperature lies beyond the 420 h axis (the value is never moved onto the edge): E-151 (500 h).

Analytical-series values are drawn only where the criterion holds: a value of the independent analytical series is exported only where (1) the time is not earlier than the series' own minimum valid time (omitted

modes below exp(-40) of their weight) and (2) the value exceeds the series' estimated absolute accuracy (about 2.2e-16 over the smallest flux ratio of the shooting solution), and is positive; otherwise it is left

empty. The early part of every BTCS curve is not converged in time: where the release is still rising steeply from zero, the base run and the run with half the step differ by a large factor, and the report states
for each curve the time after which they agree within 10 percent (a reading aid, not a tolerance). Model: STRATO BTCS five-layer spherical finite difference, package version 1.0.1, commit

c9978f0f64b04fe18f312c82c38592f36d05d2f8; registered AGR1-B-M16 geometry; published heating-test diffusion coefficients chosen by the strato-data selection function (register sets C16-T2 and C16-BUF), evaluated at
the test temperature; kernel-only start; constant temperature; decay and generation are not in the solver. This is a numerical comparison, not an experimental validation.
